title: Extension to H-free graphs
statement_text: Determine the maximum possible number of edges of an $H$-free graph on $n$ vertices with matching number at most $s$, for general forbidden subgraphs $H$ (extending the authors' solution of the case $H = K_{k+1}$).
context_text: The matching number of $G$ is the maximum size of a matching, and $H$-free means containing no (not necessarily induced) copy of $H$. Turán's theorem gives the maximum number $t(n,k)$ of edges of a graph on $n$ vertices with clique number at most $k$ (attained by the balanced complete $k$-partite Turán graph $T(n,k)$), and the Erdős–Gallai theorem the maximum number of edges with matching number at most $s$. Let $G(n,k,s)$ be the complete $k$-partite graph on $n$ vertices with $k-1$ classes of sizes as equal as possible and total size $s$, plus one class of size $n-s$, and $g(n,k,s)$ its number of edges. The authors prove the common generalization: for $n\ge2s+1$, the maximum number of edges of a graph on $n$ vertices with clique number at most $k$ (i.e. $K_{k+1}$-free) and matching number at most $s$ is $\max\{t(2s+1,k),g(n,k,s)\}$. They suggest extending this to other forbidden graphs $H$, and prove, using Simonovits's result on color-critical graphs, that if $H$ is color-critical (has an edge whose deletion decreases its chromatic number) with chromatic number $k+1>2$, then for $s>s_0(H)$ and $n>n_0(s)$ the maximum is $g(n,k,s)$. The general case (other $H$, smaller parameters) is left open.
notes: No labeled environment; posed as a research direction at the start of Section 3, partially addressed by Proposition 3.1 in the same section.
